return-on-assets.title: Use a documented average rather than two endpoints
steps: A supplied 1,500,000 average gives 120,000 / 1,500,000 = 8%.
The higher average changes the denominator; no annualization is added.

assumable-mortgage.title: Compare the same 150,000 cash contribution
assumable-mortgage.inputs: price: 450000; assumed_balance: 300000; assumed_rate: 3; remaining_months: 240; assumption_fees: 3000; new_rate: 6.5; new_months: 360; new_fees: 6000; horizon_months: 60
steps: 450,000 price − 300,000 assumed balance = 150,000 cash toward price.
Add 3,000 assumption fees for 153,000 cash at closing. The alternative uses the same down payment, plus its own fees.
assumable-mortgage.answer: Purchase price minus assumed balance: 150,000.00 under these assumptions.

assumable-mortgage.title: Borrow the remaining 100,000 gap
assumable-mortgage.inputs: price: 450000; assumed_balance: 300000; assumed_rate: 3; remaining_months: 240; assumption_fees: 3000; new_rate: 6.5; new_months: 360; new_fees: 6000; horizon_months: 60; buyer_cash: 50000; gap_rate: 9; gap_months: 120; gap_fees: 2000
steps: The alternative new mortgage is 400,000, matching total initial borrowing.
assumable-mortgage.answer: Gap loan principal: 100,000.00 under these assumptions.

assumable-mortgage.title: Ignore gap-loan charges when the gap is fully cash-funded
assumable-mortgage.inputs: price: 450000; assumed_balance: 300000; assumed_rate: 3; remaining_months: 240; assumption_fees: 3000; new_rate: 6.5; new_months: 360; new_fees: 6000; horizon_months: 60; buyer_cash: 150000; gap_rate: 9; gap_months: 120; gap_fees: 99999
steps: Buyer cash covers the full 150,000 gap, leaving zero gap principal.
No gap-loan payment, interest or fee is charged; the entered gap fee is ignored.
assumable-mortgage.answer: Gap loan principal: 0.00 under these assumptions.

assumable-mortgage.title: Track payoff at a horizon beyond the old remaining term
assumable-mortgage.inputs: price: 450000; assumed_balance: 300000; assumed_rate: 0; remaining_months: 12; assumption_fees: 0; new_rate: 0; new_months: 24; new_fees: 0; horizon_months: 24
steps: Both zero-rate loans finish by month 24.
Different payment timing does not create financing profit: interest and fees are zero on both paths.
assumable-mortgage.answer: New-loan cost minus assumption cost through horizon: 0.00 under these assumptions.

assumable-mortgage.title: Retain a negative assumption advantage when new borrowing is cheaper
assumable-mortgage.inputs: price: 450000; assumed_balance: 300000; assumed_rate: 12; remaining_months: 240; assumption_fees: 9000; new_rate: 2; new_months: 360; new_fees: 0; horizon_months: 60; buyer_cash: 50000; gap_rate: 9; gap_months: 120; gap_fees: 2000
steps: The assumed first loan has the higher note rate and fees in this hypothetical case.
The signed cost difference is negative, so the model does not present assumption as universally cheaper.
assumable-mortgage.answer: New-loan cost minus assumption cost through horizon: -183,931.83 under these assumptions.

steps: After one monthly payment, most principal remains outstanding.
